Not sure what you meant. Could you elaborate?

> Not sure what you meant. Could you elaborate?

Can a fix be done at nodeJS level (by patching zlib sources), before doing a proper fix in zlib itself (upstream)?

The problem can be reproduced with a native Windows on Arm build, so it's not related to cross compilation issue.

You can fix compilation by using this patch:
```
diff --git a/deps/zlib/zlib.gyp b/deps/zlib/zlib.gyp
index 03a763ba12..527af905f7 100644
--- a/deps/zlib/zlib.gyp
+++ b/deps/zlib/zlib.gyp
@@ -101,6 +101,11 @@
                 }]
               ],
             }],
+            ['target_arch in "arm64" and OS=="win"', {
+                'defines': ['ARMV8_OS_WINDOWS',
+                            '__ARM_NEON'],
+                'sources': ['cpu_features.c'],
+            }],
             ['arm_fpu=="neon"', {
               'defines': [
                 'ADLER32_SIMD_NEON',
```

Some details:
- `ARMV8_OS_WINDOWS` should be defined in case that `arm_fpu=="neon"`. I have no idea why we don't enter this case. Does someone know where it's supposed to come from?
- cpu_features.c checks for `__ARM_NEON` presence to define a needed function. This macro is defined for clang-cl (used by chromium/v8), but not by MSVC. This case could be added in chromium's zlib **BUT** considering NodeJS is probably the only project in the world using that library with MSVC, I think it's better to support it here and not upstream.

@richardlau Keeping support for MSVC considering upstream chromium/v8 is not actively supporting is a long and tedious path It's not the first time there is a problem because of this (see [those patches](https://groups.google.com/g/v8-dev/c/RoYs2mvWPw8/m/p-w4qivOAwAJ) that have been needed for latest v8 update). After doing all this, I really think it's not the best way to maintain and help nodeJS.

Do you think we could discuss migrating to clang-cl for building Windows variants of nodeJS? The change is pretty easy to do as it's a drop-in replacement for cl.exe and it would solve *many* future problems.

@targos Given your experience on NodeJS (and updating components), do you think pushing gn (instead of dead gyp) at the same time could be something worth and possible? IMHO, fixing build with gyp is not really the good approach, as differences will keep coming in the future.

Switching to gn would make updates absolutely on par with what chromium/v8 are doing, and would really be a good thing for NodeJS in general. By doing this, I don't see how there could be any difference when compiling with clang-cl.

I think everyone in the project would like us to drop gyp in favor of GN. What we need for it is someone who has the knowledge and time to do it. We have a dormant initiative for it: https://github.com/nodejs/build-toolchain-next/issues

> I think everyone in the project would like us to drop gyp in favor of GN. What we need for it is someone who has the knowledge and time to do it. We have a dormant initiative for it: https://github.com/nodejs/build-toolchain-next/issues

I think migrating would be worth it. We always run into issues during V8 upgrades and keeping node build to use GN and clang-cl would keep things easy.

issue_context.title: Building docs support for 32 bit Ubuntu 18.04
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I was trying to build node from source on my 32 bit Ubuntu 18.04 (experimental) and when I tried to build it by following the instructions in the docs, I ran into the same problem as discussed here: https://github.com/nodejs/help/issues/2943#issuecomment-683422131
Unfortunately, I could not really understand what I have to do to get it to work on my system.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I think it would be nice if https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/33044 was discussed in the building docs as well.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It would also be okay if https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/33044 was linked to in the building docs.

What do y'all think? :slightly_smiling_face:
